matchups.recap: Rob got absolutely skull-fucked by 8.6 points this week, and honestly, that's being generous to whatever the hell he was running out there. 126.9 points is what you'd score if you drafted exclusively from the waiver wire at 2 AM on a Tuesday and then forgot to check your lineup for four days. Veton walked in and took his lunch money without breaking a sweat, and Rob's still out here wondering if his players remembered they were supposed to play football.

Ben got absolutely obliterated this week, losing by nearly 26 points like he was trying to tank for draft position in Week 12. His roster looked like he was playing a different sport entirely—maybe darts, because every decision landed in the fucking bullseye of bad. Faton walked away laughing while Ben's team imploded harder than a wet paper bag in a thunderstorm, and now he gets to spend the rest of the week explaining to the group chat how this wasn't actually his fault.

Ilir got absolutely dad-dicked this week, limping across the finish line with 90.1 points like a three-legged dog in a thunderstorm. Ten-point-nine points isn't just a loss, it's a fucking cry for help—dude's out here playing fantasy like he's flying blind with a broken compass. Nori walked away with 101 and didn't even have to break a sweat watching Ilir's roster implode like a wet cardboard box. Time to check the waiver wire, buddy, because whatever the hell you're doing right now sure as shit ain't working.

Jetmir and Peter got absolutely dicked down 120.9 to 91.5, and honestly, that 29.4-point margin feels generous—like the league felt bad watching them get their asses handed to them and decided not to run up the score any further. Between the two of them, they couldn't put together a competent lineup if their lives depended on it, and Arben made sure everyone watching knew exactly how little these clowns belonged on the same field. This wasn't a matchup, it was a public execution.

Flamur got absolutely buttfucked by a 4.5-point margin—the fantasy equivalent of losing a game on a missed extra point while your entire roster shit the bed in unison. You had one job: outscore 99 points in a league full of your buddies, and you couldn't even clear 100 like some kind of middle-school rec league scrub. Rilind's mediocre ass walked away with a W while you're left explaining to yourself why you thought *that* was your championship team. Better luck next week, chief—you're gonna need it.

Adam got his shit pushed in by less than 3 points—the fantasy football equivalent of losing a fistfight to a toddler. You had all week to set a winning lineup and still managed to come up 2.9 points short, which means somewhere on your bench was either the guy who scored 3 points or just enough production to not completely embarrass yourself. Rinor's team showed up ready to work while you were apparently taking a nap during your flex spot decisions. Better luck next week, but let's be honest—you won't get it.

matchups.preview: Faton's cruising at 5-3 thinking he's a genius, but Rob's about to remind everyone why you don't tank your entire season in Week 2—oh wait, that ship sailed two months ago. Rob's 2-6 ass is playing for pride at this point, which means absolutely nothing when your roster looks like a waiver-wire fire sale, so expect Faton to sleepwalk through this one and still somehow win by 40.

Veton's limping in at 2-6 looking like a man who drafted with his eyes closed, and now he's got the audacity to face someone actually treading water at .500? Ilir's mediocre record is still a masterclass compared to whatever dumpster fire Veton's been running—this is less of a matchup and more of a mercy killing. Don't worry Veton, at least you'll have plenty of Sundays free to think about where it all went wrong.

Ben's sitting at 3-5 because apparently he thought "league winner" meant "league loser," and now he's desperately hoping his waiver wire lottery tickets finally hit so he can pretend this season wasn't a complete disaster. Meanwhile, Jetmir and Peter are actually treading water at .500, which is still somehow better than Ben's dumpster fire—but don't get comfortable, because you two are about to get exposed by a guy who's already got nothing to lose.

Nori's sitting pretty at 5-3, but let's be real—that record is held together with duct tape and prayer, and this week Rilind's about to bring the scissors. Sure, Rilind's been an absolute dumpster fire at 2-6, but even a blind squirrel finds a nut, and Nori's roster is about as reliable as a screen door on a submarine. Time for Rilind to accidentally stumble into a win and remind everyone why Nori's "winning" record is basically a participation trophy.

Arben's coasting on a 7-1 record like he actually knows what he's doing, but we all remember how he choked last year—dude's due for a catastrophic collapse and this is the week the wheels fall off. Adam's sitting at 3-5 playing desperate football, which honestly might be the only thing keeping him from being completely irrelevant, but let's be real: he's about to get bulldozed by a team that actually has their shit together.

Flamur's sitting pretty at 6-2 thinking he's hot shit, but we all know that record's held together with duct tape and prayer—one bad week and this house of cards collapses faster than his draft strategy did. Rinor's lurking at 5-3 like a hungry dog, and if there's one thing we know about this matchup, it's that Flamur chokes when it matters; expect another classic collapse where his "studs" disappear and Rinor sneaks through with a W that he'll talk about until next draft day.
